**Company Description**
The Wonderful Company is committed to providing high-quality, healthy, and iconic brands, including FIJI Water, POM Wonderful, Wonderful Pistachios, Wonderful Halos and helping improve the lives of the people who live and work in the places where we operate. Ranked No. 1 on the 2025 PEOPLE® Companies That Care list and one of Fortune® magazine’s “100 Best Companies to Work For” in the U.S., The Wonderful Company is continually recognized for its dedication to the well-being of its workforce, their communities, and the planet.
  
  
Since 1996, FIJI Water has embodied what it means to be Earth's Finest Water®. Sourced from the islands of Fiji, FIJI Water is the No. 1 premium imported bottled water brand in the United States, and America’s Favorite Bottled Water Brand. FIJI Water is sold in more than 80 countries worldwide, known for its iconic square bottle, unique mineral profile, and soft smooth taste. Sourced from a natural artesian aquifer in the islands of Fiji, the difference is the source – FIJI Water gathers natural electrolytes and minerals and maintains a perfectly balanced pH.
  
  
FIJI Water is committed to doing business responsibly and seeking opportunities to make a difference. That commitment extends to the FIJI Water Foundation – one of the largest philanthropic organizations in Fiji – which focuses its efforts and investments on education, clean water access, environmental sustainability, health and wellness, emergency relief, and community development.
  
  
The Director of Strategy and Continuous Improvement (CI) collaborates with executive leaders to identify and tackle pressing strategic challenges, develop growth strategies, enhance operational and technological efficiencies utilizing lean principles to deliver financial and organizational benefits. This position will develop and utilize its holistic team, including a Project Management Office, and partner with functional areas within FIJI Water to support the ongoing growth of the brand. Areas of focus include: Supply Chain, Operations, Production, Maintenance & Reliability, Quality, HR, Finance, Sales and Management Infrastructure.
  
  
**Up to 25% travel is required in this role, both internationally to Fiji and domestically within the United States.**
This position will be based at our West Los Angeles, CA office. We work a hybrid schedule with an in-office requirement Monday-Wednesday and the option to work remotely on Thursday and Friday.
  
  
**Job Description**

* Lead high-impact strategic, commercial, and operational initiatives from concept through implementation, ensuring successful execution and measurable business results.
* Develop and execute strategic plans that support long-term business priorities and operational excellence.
* Build strong partnerships with senior leaders to identify opportunities, align stakeholders, and drive organizational change.
* Lead, develop, and mentor the Continuous Improvement team, prioritizing work across multiple initiatives to maximize business impact and supporting travel and on-site work as needed.
* Oversee the FIJI Water Project Management Office (PMO), ensuring effective project governance, portfolio management, and execution via Senior Manager of PMO.
* Develop organizational Continuous Improvement capabilities through coaching, training, workshops, and leadership development.
* Champion Lean, problem-solving, and change management methodologies to improve processes, eliminate waste, and build a culture of continuous improvement.
* Lead cross-functional teams to investigate business challenges, identify root causes, and implement sustainable process improvements and best practices.
* Establish standardized processes, performance measures, and management systems that improve operational effectiveness and scalability.
* Build and maintain a network of cross-functional subject matter experts within and outside the FIJI Water organization.
* Travel as needed to support business partners, project execution, and organizational development initiatives, including domestic and international travel.

**Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10-15 years of relevant experience in strategy, consulting, operations, technology, finance, or a related field, including 5 years of people management experience.
* MBA or equivalent graduate degree preferred.
* Demonstrable executive presence.
* Experience managing team members and developing junior employees.
* Exceptional problem-solving skills, especially in ambiguous or undefined situations.
* Proactive, self-starter attitude with a track record of taking initiative.
* Strong leadership and team management capabilities.
* Excellent communication skills and the ability to build effective partnerships.
* Willingness and ability to travel as required.

Pay Range: $190,000 - $220,000 and may include a discretionary bonus. Final compensation will be dependent upon skills & experience.
  
  
**Additional Information**

* Thriving Wellness Community: Access to top-notch medical coverage comprehensive vision and dental plans, and a 401k with match eligibility to secure your financial future and including:

+ 24/7 online physician consultations
+ virtual mental health resources
+ life coaching
+ engaging employee community groups
+ cash rewards for healthy habits and fitness reimbursements
+ library of on-demand fitness videos

* Career Advancement Opportunities: Unlock your potential with clear paths for career progression and internal mobility across our diverse family of brands and business units.
* Focused Learning and Development: Grow as a leader with our dedicated Learning and Organizational Development department, offering extensive resources like People Manager and leadership training, webinars, and eLearning courses.
* Empowering Mentorship Program: Connect with colleagues through our company-wide mentorship program to share goals, overcome challenges, and drive your career forward.
* Continuous Improvement Training: Participate in training that empowers all employees to learn and implement concepts that drive significant, positive change in the workplace.
* Building a Healthy Society: To date, our co-Founders Lynda and Stewart Resnick, through their foundations and The Wonderful Company, have invested more than $2.5 billion in education, health and wellness, community development, and sustainability initiatives across California’s Central Valley, Fiji, and the world. In 2025, Wonderful ranked as #1 in PEOPLE’s “100 Companies That Care” list and was named one of Fortune magazine’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. To learn more about our corporate social responsibility efforts, visit csr.wonderful.com.
* Giving Back to the Community: Make a difference with Wonderful Giving, allowing you to allocate company-provided funds to up to three charities of your choice, and join Wonderful Neighbor to contribute to group service projects within our local communities.

FIJI® Water is a natural artesian water bottled at the source in Viti Levu (Fiji Islands). With its iconic square bottle, soft mouthfeel, and more than double the electrolytes of the other two top premium bottled water brands, FIJI Water is the No. 1 premium imported bottled water in the United States. FIJI Water has a perfectly balanced 7.7pH. FIJI Water is available in a variety of sizes, including 330mL, 500mL, 700mL, 700mL Sports Cap, 1L, and 1.5L.
  
  
As part of its longstanding commitment to sustainability, nearly 70% of FIJI Water’s global bottle volume is in 100% recycled plastic (rPET), including its best-selling 500mL and 330mL bottles. Since 2007, the FIJI Water Foundation has been committed to supporting environmental conservation and strengthening local communities, investing more than USD $20.5 million in community development, access to safe water, education, health & wellness, and environmental sustainability.
  
  
To discover Earth’s Finest Water®, please visit www.fijiwater.com, like us on Facebook, or follow us on Instagram.

The strongest candidate will bring hands-on manufacturing and industrials performance improvement experience, including plant operations leadership, enterprise value creation, CAPEX execution, Lean/Six Sigma, value stream performance, labor productivity, safety, quality, and operational transformation. records.title: Director of Quality and Accreditation
records.description:
Overview:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
  + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
  + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
  + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
  + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
  + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
  + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
  + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
  + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
  + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
  + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
  + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
  + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
  + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
  + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
    - Changes in policies/procedures,
    - Staffing and assignment changes,
    - Additional education or training for staff,
    - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

***While this job description is intended to be*** ***an accurate*** ***reflection of the requirements of the job, management reserves the right to add or remove duties from*** ***par******ticular jobs*** ***when circumstances***  
***(******e.g.*** ***emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.***

The Director, Quality Operations is a hands-on, results-driven operator responsible for disciplined, scalable execution across HEDIS, Stars, clinical quality programs, and the In-Home Assessment (IHA) program. Reporting to the Senior Director, Quality, this role provides operational leadership for the Quality Operations team and directly oversees the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations. The Director serves as the critical connection point between the centralized operations team and regional and market teams, between operations and technology, and alongside the Payor team with our health plan partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, and work gets done. This role is built for a strong operator with a bias for action: someone who brings structure to complexity, holds teams and partners accountable, closes loops, and consistently delivers measurable improvement in quality results.

**Essential Job Function**s:

**1. Operational Leadership and Execution**

Lead the day-to-day operating model for enterprise quality programs, including HEDIS, Stars, ACO/MSSP quality initiatives, clinical quality programs, and the IHA program.

Execute priorities set by the Senior Director through annual operating plans, workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Directly manage and develop the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations, and provide leadership across the broader quality operations team.

Serve as the primary liaison between the centralized Quality Operations team and regional and market teams, ensuring enterprise priorities, workflows, and expectations are clearly communicated, adopted, and executed locally, and that market needs, barriers, and feedback are surfaced and resolved centrally.

Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence, including action-item tracking, issue logs, escalation paths, and KPI scorecards, so that commitments are owned, deadlines are met, and open items are driven to closure.

**2. IHA Program Oversig**ht

Own end-to-end operational oversight of the IHA program, including implementation planning, workflow design, market readiness, vendor coordination, KPI monitoring, and issue resolution.

Partner with market, clinical, analytics, coding, risk adjustment, and health plan teams to ensure IHA activities support quality and clinical objectives.

Monitor IHA program productivity, completion, quality, member experience, documentation, and downstream outcomes; implement corrective actions when results are below target.

Drive consistent IHA execution across regions and markets, holding vendors and internal partners accountable to targets and ensuring identified gaps and follow-up needs are closed.

**3. Quality Program Operation**s

Ensure operational readiness for HEDIS/Stars submissions, audits, roadmaps and health plan deliverables.

Coordinate enterprise and market-level quality calendars, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across cross-functional teams.

Drive continuous improvement by evaluating workflows, identifying root causes, and implementing scalable solutions.

Serve as the liaison between Quality Operations and the Technology and Product teams, translating operational needs into clearly defined business requirements, use cases, and success measures.

Lead prioritization of quality-related technology requests and enhancements based on quality impact, operational risk, and timing; maintain a transparent backlog and roadmap in partnership with Technology.

Track delivery of technology work against committed timelines, coordinate user acceptance testing and rollout with operations and market users, and escalate risks or delays as needed.

**5. Health Plan Partnershi**p

Work alongside the Payor team to track, manage, and follow up on open health plan items, requests, and deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution.

Attend and actively participate in health plan meetings, including Joint Operating Committees (JOCs) and quality working sessions, to build strong partnerships with health plan partners and drive quality results.

Lead operational discussions with health plans on quality programs, data exchange and supplemental data, gap closure, and quality results; ensure action items from health plan meetings are documented and completed.

Maintain a consolidated view of health plan quality commitments, programs, and incentive opportunities across markets to inform prioritization and resource planning.

**6. Stakeholder and Vendor Managemen**t

Build collaborative relationships with Regional Quality, Market, Payor, Clinical, Analytics, Coding, Risk Adjustment, Technology, Product, Finance, and other enterprise partners.

Lead operational discussions with vendors and external partners; monitor results against service levels, quality standards, and contractual commitments.

* Demonstrate excellent communication, customer service, attention to detail, and accountability.
* Travel as required.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

**Minimum Experience**

* Minimum of 9 years of applicable healthcare quality, clinical operations, or program operations experience, including at least 3 years of people management experience.

As the **Head of Quality,** you will leader to define, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System across the Americas. This role is responsible for ensuring quality is designed into every stage of project delivery, from engineering and procurement through construction, commissioning, and closeout. This is a highly visible leadership role with direct influence on project performance, supplier quality, operational discipline, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the Americas.

The **Head of Quality** will establish and lead a quality organization that embeds quality into how projects are planned, executed, and continuously improved.

You will drive a preventive approach to quality by strengthening planning, supplier oversight, project controls, auditing, and lessons learned. You will create the frameworks that connect Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Delivery, and Quality into a single system focused on delivering projects right the first time. Success will be measured by reductions in rework and recurring issues, stronger supplier performance, improved audit outcomes, increased first-time-right execution, and the maturity of the quality culture across the organization.

**What will you do?**

  

* You will lead the development and continuous improvement of the Americas Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring consistent standards, governance, and accountability across the region.
* You will establish quality requirements and controls from tender through project closeout to ensure quality is built into project delivery from the outset.
* You will implement risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, and release processes to improve supplier quality performance.
* You will ensure inspection and test plans align with engineering requirements, contract obligations, and construction execution strategies.
* You will lead audits, management reviews, quality assurance programs, and performance reporting across the project portfolio.

* You will improve audit performance, supplier quality outcomes, and project readiness before execution begins.
* You will create a culture where quality is proactively planned, owned, measured, and continuously improved across functions.
* You will build a scalable quality organization capable of supporting Linxon's continued growth across the Americas.

**Who you are?**

  

* You are an experienced quality leader with 7-15+ years of experience in EPC, power, industrial, construction, manufacturing, or other complex project environments.
* You are proven in leading multi-project or regional Quality Management Systems and driving quality performance across diverse operations.

* You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting course as conditions change.
* You are committed to raising standards while fostering respect, inclusion, and psychological safety.

records.description:
About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.
* Coordinate production readiness with Engineering, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.
* Ensure aircraft move smoothly from production through acceptance and delivery.

  

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Ensure compliance with FAA Part 21 production requirements and the company quality management system.
* Maintain production configuration control and manufacturing documentation discipline.
* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.
* Partner with Quality leadership to improve first-pass yield.

  

**Growth and scale-up**

* Develop the manufacturing infrastructure, facilities and staffing plans needed for higher production rates.
* Implement lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.

  

**People leadership**

* Recruit, develop and mentor production leaders and technical staff.
* Establish workforce development and skills-training programs.
* Build strong partnerships across Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.

  

Success Measures

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production schedule attainment, factory throughput, labor productivity, manufacturing cost, quality and first-pass yield, safety, production-rate readiness, and workforce development and retention.

Required Qualifications

  

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Aerospace, Operations or a related technical field.
* 15+ years of progressive aerospace manufacturing leadership experience, including 10+ years leading production organizations in aerospace, defense, aviation or another highly regulated industry.
* Proven experience scaling manufacturing from development, prototype or low-rate production to higher-rate production.
* Experience leading large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations.
* Strong understanding of production planning, factory operations, quality systems and manufacturing performance metrics.
* Experience implementing lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.
* Excellent communication, leadership and organizational skills.

  

Preferred Qualifications

  

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business or Operations.

* Experience leading final assembly and aircraft integration organizations.
* Experience supporting aircraft certification, conformity and production acceptance.
* Background in autonomous aircraft, UAS, defense aviation or advanced aerospace systems.

**Director of Manufacturing**
=============================

Baton Rouge, LA | Full-Time | On-Site

**About Us**

Safe Air Technology is a rapidly growing manufacturer of mission-critical and explosion-proof HVAC systems. We take pride in building high-quality, precision-engineered equipment and are looking for skilled individuals who take pride in their workmanship.

**Position Summary**

Safe Air Technology is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Manufacturing to lead and oversee all aspects of our manufacturing operations. This is a senior leadership position responsible for driving production performance, operational efficiency, quality, safety, and workforce accountability across our manufacturing facilities.

The ideal candidate is a strong, hands-on manufacturing leader with extensive experience managing complex production environments, developing high-performing teams, and implementing processes that support rapid growth and increased production capacity.

Reporting directly to the Vice President of Manufacturing, this individual will provide strategic and operational leadership to ensure manufacturing objectives are achieved while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Manufacturing Operations & Production Leadership

* Direct and oversee daily manufacturing operations across all production departments, ensuring alignment with company goals and production schedules.
* Lead production managers, supervisors, and department leaders to achieve manufacturing targets and operational objectives.
* Establish clear performance expectations, accountability measures, and production standards throughout the organization.
* Ensure effective coordination between manufacturing departments to maintain consistent workflow and eliminate production bottlenecks.
* Monitor production schedules, capacity, labor utilization, and output to ensure on-time delivery of customer orders.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing to develop and execute operational strategies supporting business growth and increased production demand.
* Oversee the successful implementation and management of multiple shifts as production requirements evolve.

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, efficiency, quality, cost reduction, and operational performance.
* Identify manufacturing inefficiencies, process gaps, and workflow constraints, implementing sustainable corrective actions.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including production output, labor efficiency, schedule attainment, rework, and on-time delivery.
* Implement standardized processes, procedures, and performance expectations across manufacturing departments.
* Apply Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies to optimize production operations.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes that support increased production volume without compromising quality or safety.

Leadership & Workforce Development

* Provide leadership, coaching, and development to production managers, supervisors, and manufacturing personnel.
* Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
* Partner with Human Resources to identify staffing needs, workforce development opportunities, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing levels, and supervisory coverage to ensure appropriate resources are in place.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, attendance, productivity, and adherence to company policies.
* Develop strong frontline leadership capable of independently managing daily production activities.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

* Promote a safety-first culture and ensure compliance with company safety policies, OSHA regulations, and applicable manufacturing standards.
* Partner with Quality and Safety leadership to reduce defects, rework, incidents, and operational risks.
* Ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet engineering specifications, quality requirements, and customer expectations.
* Drive accountability for workmanship, quality standards, and adherence to established procedures.
* Support root cause analysis and corrective action initiatives to prevent recurring quality or production issues.

Financial & Resource Management

* Manage manufacturing performance with a strong focus on labor costs, overtime, productivity, and operational efficiency.
* Monitor resource utilization and recommend improvements to optimize manufacturing costs.
* Partner with Finance and executive leadership to support manufacturing budgets, labor planning, capital expenditures, and cost-control initiatives.
* Evaluate equipment, facility, staffing, and technology needs to support operational growth.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing profitability through better resource allocation, process improvements, and increased productivity.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Strategic Execution

* Collaborate closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Project Management, Human Resources, and Finance to ensure alignment of manufacturing priorities.
* Partner with Supply Chain to address material availability, inventory constraints, and production readiness.
* Work with Engineering to resolve technical challenges, improve manufacturability, and minimize production disruptions.
* Provide regular manufacturing performance updates, operational risks, and improvement recommendations to the VP of Manufacturing and executive leadership.
* Support facility expansions, production transitions, new product introductions, and other strategic manufacturing initiatives.
* Translate company objectives into actionable manufacturing plans with measurable results.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred. Equivalent experience will be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including at least 5 years in a senior management or director-level role.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing large-scale manufacturing operations with multiple departments, production teams, and supervisory personnel.
* Proven success improving production output, operational efficiency, labor productivity, and manufacturing performance.
* Strong understanding of production planning, capacity management, manufacturing cost controls, and operational KPIs.
* Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement initiatives, and standardized production processes.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment with changing priorities and demanding production schedules.
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing reporting tools.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience in HVAC manufacturing, industrial equipment, electrical integration, engineered-to-order products, or complex industrial manufacturing.
* Experience managing multi-shift manufacturing operations.
* Background in manufacturing environments involving mechanical assembly, electrical systems, refrigeration, fabrication, and equipment testing.
* Demonstrated success scaling manufacturing operations during periods of significant business growth.
* Experience supporting facility expansions, operational restructuring, and manufacturing process improvements.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or related continuous improvement training.

**Key Performance Expectations**
--------------------------------

Success in this role will be measured by the ability to:

* Production Performance: Consistently achieve established manufacturing output and delivery targets.
* Operational Efficiency: Improve labor productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Quality: Reduce rework, defects, and production-related quality issues.
* Safety: Maintain a safe working environment and strengthen safety accountability.
* Leadership: Develop effective production managers and supervisors who consistently deliver results.
* Cost Management: Control labor expenses, overtime, and manufacturing costs while supporting production demand.
* Continuous Improvement: Implement measurable process improvements that support long-term operational growth.

**Leadership Expectations**
---------------------------

The Director of Manufacturing must be a visible, engaged leader who takes ownership of shop performance. This individual should be comfortable spending time on the manufacturing floor, addressing challenges directly, making timely decisions, and holding leaders accountable for results.

We are looking for someone who can balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, build strong teams, and bring the structure, discipline, and leadership necessary to support Safe Air Technology's continued growth.

**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; understand highly regulatory issues (current and proposed) and appropriate permitting for solid waste facilities, recycling operations and programs; negotiate with the best interest of ReGen Monterey; work independently with minimal supervision; manage and evaluate the work of others; prepare clear and concise plans, specifications, and technical reports; interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations; present proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively in public meetings; develop and implement appropriate procedures and controls; exercise sound, independent judgment within policy guidelines; develop and administer departmental goals, objectives, and procedures; analyze and assess programs, policies, and operational needs and make appropriate adjustments; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods and techniques; facilitate group participation and consensus building; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of or ability to obtain a certificate of Manager of Landfill Operations (MOLO) issued by the Solid Waste Association of North America (SWANA) is desired.
* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**PhYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:**

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret complex data, information and documents; analyze and solve complex policy and operational problems; observe and interpret people and situations; use math and mathematical reasoning; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with constant interruptions; work under intensive deadlines and interact with Board members, all levels of ReGen Monterey management, other elected and appointed governmental officials, consultants, contractors, developers, vendors, employees, media representatives and the public.

**Special Demands**

Must be able to actively participate in public meetings, including giving presentations in person and on camera before the Board of Directors and members of the public.

**Work Environment**

Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet, occasional exposure to dirt, grease, foul odors and other outdoor elements.

records.description:
**Position Summary**  
The Director of Value-Add Manufacturing oversees all value-added manufacturing operations, ensuring safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives are consistently achieved. This role provides strategic leadership for manufacturing activities including machining, fabrication, assembly, kitting, packaging, finishing, and custom processing operations. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence through process improvement, workforce development, cross-functional collaboration, and execution of manufacturing strategies that support company growth and customer satisfaction.  
  
**Essential Duties/Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership: Develop manufacturing strategies, capacity plans, growth initiatives, performance goals, and operational roadmaps aligned with company objectives.
* Operational Management: Direct machining, fabrication, assembly, kitting, packaging, finishing, production scheduling, labor planning, equipment utilization, and workflow optimization.
* Safety & Compliance: Lead safety programs, OSHA compliance, environmental compliance, facility audits, risk reduction, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Quality Assurance: Drive quality systems, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, defect reduction, scrap reduction, and customer satisfaction.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, process optimization, waste elimination, productivity improvement, and operational excellence initiatives.
* Financial Management: Manage operating budgets, capital expenditures, cost reduction programs, ROI analysis, and profitability improvement initiatives.
* Team Leadership: Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing managers, supervisors, and manufacturing personnel while supporting succession planning.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engineering, Sales, Procurement, Distribution, and Customer Service to align manufacturing capabilities with business requirements.
* Key Performance Metrics: Safety, On-Time Delivery, OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness), Throughput, Labor Productivity, First Pass Yield, Scrap Reduction, Inventory Turns, Cost Performance, Customer Satisfaction, and EBITDA improvement.

**Qualifications**  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.  
  
**Education**

* Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or related discipline required. MBA preferred. Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, APICS/ASCM, or related certifications preferred.

**Experience/Skills/Abilities Required**

* 10-15 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years leading managers and supervisors.
* Experience managing machining, fabrication, assembly, and value-added manufacturing operations.
* Strong Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement experience.
* Experience with ERP systems, production planning, inventory management, and KPI reporting.
* Strong financial acumen including budgeting, forecasting, cost management, and capital planning.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to build effective relationships across all levels of the organization.

**Work Environment/Physical Demands**  
Noise levels may be high at times. Position requires regular presence in office and manufacturing environments. Standing, walking, sitting, reaching, stooping, bending, pushing, pulling, and occasional lifting up to 50 pounds may be required. Appropriate PPE must be worn when required.

records.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations
records.description:
**Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations**

*Own the supply chain and CMC project engine behind Nurix's clinical programs and commercial readiness. In this multifaceted role, you will select and manage CMOs, keep clinical supply flowing to trial sites around the world, and drive cross-functional CMC plans from early development toward commercialization, in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities.*

  

**Position Description**

The position is a multifaceted role supporting several areas within the Technical Operations group, including supply chain management, CMC project management, and clinical labeling and distribution. The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and self-directed, with experience and interest in working in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities and opportunities.

  

**The Opportunity**

* Lead the effort to identify, select, and manage Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) for the development and cGMP manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and DS in support of ongoing clinical programs and commercial products (with finance and commercial teams)
* Manage global supply chains and logistics in support of demand for clinical studies and commercial products
* Working in conjunction with technical teams, provide vendor management support in all logistics and operations to ensure on-time delivery of materials
* Coordinate the design and execution of cross-functional CMC project plans and budgeting for early clinical development through commercial readiness
* Maintain frequent communication with cross-functional CMC project team members and key internal stakeholders so that all parties are aware of current project status, issues, contingencies, milestones, and budgets
* Proactively identify the CMC critical path, risks, and impediments to successful development, and drive the identification and development of solutions to mitigate these risks
* Serve as primary clinical supply chain contact, working collaboratively with internal and external partners
* Manage clinical supply planning and forecasting for study protocols and develop packaging/labeling and global distribution strategies
* Monitor IXRS portal processes, including high and low enrolling site settings, drug acknowledgement, depot and site supply levels, and IMP status of released lots or expired drug
* Coordinate the preparation and/or review of CMC sections of INDs, CTAs, NDAs, MAAs, and other regulatory submissions to ensure timely distribution of clinical trial materials
* Coordinate the process validation programs to support commercialization
* Initiate and manage high-value intercontinental, cross-border, and domestic shipments
* Coordinate the preparation, review, editing, and approval of cGMP batch records and CMC regulatory and Quality documents
* Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

  

**What You'll Bring**

* BS with 15+ years' experience; degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* At least 10 years of relevant experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology CMC/cGMP environment
* Excellent project management skills and the ability to work cross-functionally to develop and execute project plans
* Experience managing US and international CRO/CMOs for the manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and cGMP DS and DP for programs in development
* Experience with clinical supply chain, including forecasting supply needs
* Experience with cGMP manufacturing and IND, CTA, and NDA filings; thorough knowledge of relevant FDA and EMEA regulations
* Experience in supply chain management, and experience establishing pharmaceutical supply chain systems and networks
* Able to identify and resolve critical issues
* Sufficient technical background and experience to work closely with other technical functional areas
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and exceptional interpersonal and management skills to collaborate with others on assigned projects (including both internal teams and external collaborators)
* Bonus: Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* Bonus: Experience managing US and international CMOs for commercial programs

  

**Salary Range:** $270,300 - $295,700

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

  

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

  

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

  

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine's next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.*

records.title: Director, Compute Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing
records.description:
Meta is seeking a Director of Compute Manufacturing and Strategic Sourcing to lead the strategy, execution, and organizational development of our compute hardware manufacturing and supply chain functions. This role sits at the intersection of large-scale data center infrastructure and advanced manufacturing operations, driving the end-to-end readiness of compute systems — including servers, accelerators, and custom silicon-based hardware — from design through high-volume production. You will shape sourcing strategy for critical compute components, build deep partnerships with contract manufacturers and component suppliers, and ensure Meta's infrastructure hardware scales reliably to meet the demands of AI, machine learning, and global platform workloads.  
  
  

### **Director, Compute Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing Responsibilities:**

* Define and execute the manufacturing and strategic sourcing roadmap for Meta's compute and network hardware portfolio, including servers, accelerators, and custom silicon-integrated systems
* Lead supplier selection, qualification, and development for compute components and contract manufacturing partners, ensuring capacity, quality, and cost targets are met at scale
* Serve as an executive point of contact and relationship owner for key ODM & Supplier partners
* Drive design for manufacturability initiatives in partnership with hardware engineering teams to ensure compute platforms are optimized for high-volume production from early design stages
* Establish and govern manufacturing readiness processes across new product introduction phases, from prototype builds through mass production ramp up
* Develop and manage strategic sourcing frameworks for critical compute supply chains, including commodity management, dual-sourcing strategies, and long-term supply agreements
* Lead cross-functional programs spanning hardware engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations to align manufacturing execution with infrastructure deployment timelines
* Define and track key manufacturing and sourcing metrics, including yield, cost per unit, supplier on-time delivery, and supply risk exposure
* Build and scale a globally distributed team of sourcing managers, and program leads, providing technical direction and career development
* Partner with silicon and hardware architecture teams to influence component and platform decisions based on supply availability, manufacturability, and total cost of ownership
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives across the computer supply base, applying lean manufacturing principles and data-driven analysis to improve efficiency and resilience

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, strategic sourcing, or supply chain management within the compute hardware, data center infrastructure, or consumer electronics industry
* 8+ years of people management experience leading multi-disciplinary teams including engineering, sourcing, and program management functions
* Experience managing end-to-end new product introduction for complex compute hardware systems such as servers, accelerators, storage platforms, or custom silicon-integrated products
* Experience developing and executing strategic sourcing programs for compute components including processors, memory, power delivery systems, or printed circuit board assemblies
* Demonstrated track record of building and scaling supplier partnerships and contract manufacturing relationships for high-volume hardware production

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with custom silicon or ASIC-integrated compute platform manufacturing, including packaging technologies such as advanced SiP or chiplet-based architectures
* Experience applying lean manufacturing or Six Sigma methodologies to drive yield improvement and cost reduction across a global supply base
* Familiarity with data center hardware qualification processes, reliability testing methodologies, and infrastructure deployment operations
* Background in AI or machine learning infrastructure hardware, including GPU or custom accelerator supply chains

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics.  
  
  

Meta is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Meta participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law. Please note that Meta may leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in connection with applications for employment.
  
  
Meta is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance or accommodations due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations-ext@meta.com.  
  
$260,000/year to $319,000/year + bonus + equity + benefits  
  
Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Compensation details listed in this posting reflect the base hourly rate, monthly rate, or annual salary only, and do not include bonus, equity or sales incentives, if applicable. The ideal candidate is a proven cement manufacturing leader with extensive experience managing plant operations, including production, maintenance and reliability, quality, engineering, process optimization, safety, environmental compliance, and capital projects. This individual will combine strong technical knowledge of cement manufacturing with business and financial acumen, including experience managing operating and capital budgets, improving equipment reliability and plant efficiency, and controlling manufacturing costs. We are looking for a visible, hands-on leader who develops strong teams, drives accountability, and has a demonstrated ability to improve safety, reliability, quality, production, and overall plant performance.
  
  
**Who we are:**  
GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.
  
  
**What you will do:**  
Directs, coordinates and administers all production, quality control, maintenance, engineering, purchasing and process control activities required in meeting the operations budget objectives and maintains alignment with the strategic plans of GCCA for the preservation of the plant's physical assets and to meet projected sales goals. * Plans and direct the plant machinery and mobile equipment preventive maintenance program and all major maintenance projects and activities.
* Plans and directs the expenditures of the capital program.

* Hires, counsels, and trains assigned personnel, set individual goals, evaluates performance, recommends salary adjustments, promotion or transfer, approves time-off, and accomplishes objectives through the qualities of strong leadership.

* Promotes organization in industry, manufacturing or trade associations, Chamber of Commerce and community charities and agencies.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**PLANT MANAGER**

**Icon Fixtures | Multi-Facility Manufacturing Operations | St. Louis Area (Hazelwood, MO)**

About Icon

Icon Fixtures designs and builds custom fixtures, millwork, and full environments for retail, restaurant, hospitality, banking, and museum clients across North America and internationally, from single-store orders to 100+ location rollouts. Our in-house production centers on custom wood cabinetry and architectural millwork, along with metal fabrication and solid surface components.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Plant Manager to lead manufacturing, warehouse, and assembly operations across three local facilities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you will oversee approximately 30 employees through supervisors and team leaders, with significant room to grow the organization as we expand.

This is a role for a builder. The right leader will establish the scheduling systems, standards, and leadership structure that allow Icon to scale without sacrificing quality.

What You Will Do

* Lead manufacturing across all three facilities, including woodworking, cabinetry, millwork, metal, solid surface, finishing, and assembly.

* Build and own production schedules that reflect project deadlines, material availability, labor capacity, and equipment, and identify problems before they affect delivery.

* Run warehouse and assembly operations: receiving, inventory control, material flow between facilities, and preparation for shipment and installation.

* Coordinate material purchasing and production priorities with project management, engineering, and logistics.

* Develop supervisors and team leaders into a management team that runs daily operations independently; recruit, train, and retain skilled employees.

* Set and enforce quality standards against shop drawings and specifications, and reduce defects, rework, and waste.

* Manage labor costs, overtime, and operating budgets; track KPIs and report on performance, capacity, and staffing.
