records.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good. 

 At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

 Your Impact 

 You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.

 As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.

 Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.

 What You’ll Do 

 Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
 Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
 Direct Reports:   Individual Contributors

 Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers

 
 Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments

 Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments

 Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact

 Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership

 Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability

 Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders

 
 Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes

 
 Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution

 Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed

 Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption

 Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design

 Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable

 
 Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio

 
 Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs

 Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment

 Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse

 Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership

 Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook

 
 Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery

 
 Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning

 Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified

 Establish expectations for validation, observability, fallback paths, maintainability, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive data

 Ensure solutions uphold CJIS requirements, evidence integrity, privacy, approved-tooling standards, and other applicable security controls

 Encourage practical use of AI to accelerate work while preserving human ownership of architecture, accuracy, and outcomes

 
 Turn Field Learning Into Organizational Leverage

 
 Build mechanisms for Mission Engineers to document and share reusable workflows, integrations, frameworks, and playbooks

 Identify patterns across agencies and help convert successful one-off solutions into repeatable capabilities

 Create strong feedback loops with Product and Engineering around recurring workflow friction, unmet operational needs, and product opportunities

 Partner with Mission Operators, Customer Success, Deployment, Professional Services, Support, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement so agencies experience coordinated execution

 Share portfolio insights with senior leaders to influence investment, prioritization, staffing, and the evolution of the Mission Engineering operating model

 
 Lead Executive and Agency Engagement

 
 Build trusted relationships with command staff, agency executives, technical leaders, and internal senior leadership

 Serve as a senior partner during agency-impacting incidents, high-visibility deployments, and moments that require clear trade-offs or executive alignment

 Translate complex technical and operational issues into decisions that are clear to both technical teams and executive audiences

 Coach Mission Engineers to challenge requests constructively, communicate candidly, and leave stakeholders with a practical path forward

 
 What You Bring

 Required

 
 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical delivery, systems integration, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, operational transformation, or comparable environments

 5+ years leading and developing senior technical individual contributors in customer-facing organizations

 Demonstrated success coaching teams that deliver secure, production-ready solutions in complex customer environments

 Experience leading distributed or field-based teams across multiple customers, regions, or engagement models

 A record of improving technical execution, adoption, operational outcomes, and delivery consistency across a portfolio

 Broad technical fluency across SaaS platforms, cloud services, APIs, networking, hardware, integrations, data workflows, and AI-enabled technologies

 Executive presence with the ability to earn trust, communicate trade-offs, and guide decisions with command staff and senior leaders

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to distinguish isolated issues from patterns that require a scalable solution

 A data-informed leadership approach using baselines, production delivery, adoption, operational improvement, quality, and reuse to evaluate performance

 Comfort leading through ambiguity while creating clarity around ownership, priorities, and success criteria

 Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and exercise sound judgment with highly sensitive information

 
 Preferred

 
 Experience in public safety, law enforcement, defense, government technology, or another mission-critical operating environment

 Familiarity with CAD, RMS, digital evidence, real-time operations, or integrated public safety ecosystems

 Experience leading teams that build automations, integrations, operational workflows, internal tools, or AI-enabled solutions

 Experience converting field-developed solutions into reusable frameworks, product improvements, or organizational playbooks

 Familiarity with technical talent development, competency frameworks, or academy-style enablement programs

 
 Additional Information

 We recognize that leaders may arrive through different paths. If you have developed technically curious customer-facing teams, helped people turn ambiguous operational problems into working solutions, and care deeply about measurable customer impact, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits that Benefit You

 
 Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

 Discretionary paid time off

 Paid parental leave for all

 Medical, Dental, Vision plans

 Fitness Programs

 Emotional & Mental Wellness support

 Learning & Development programs

 And yes, we have snacks in our offices

 
  

 Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Important Notes 

 The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions. 

 Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment. 

 We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com  or via our  Axon Privacy Web Form . For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our  Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice. 

 Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment. 

 We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes. 

 Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers .  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com , or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com .

records.title: Director of Industrialization
records.description:
About the Company 

 We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

 The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

 About the Job 

 Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

 Panthalassa is moving from pilot production into volume manufacturing, and we are hiring a Director of Industrialization to stand up the production lines that get us there. You will own the manufacturing strategy, equipment definition, commissioning schedule, and production ramp for our new factories — the work that turns a proven pilot process and a rate target into a qualified, running line.

 This is the person who decides what we build with, how the line is configured, how long installation and commissioning will take, and how quickly the factory can climb to rate. Working with Pilot Manufacturing, you will translate product designs and proven pilot processes into a build strategy, then select and procure major capital equipment, sequence installation and qualification against a hard schedule, and define the ramp curve the rest of the business plans against.

 This role starts as an individual contributor and grows into a leadership role . For the first phase you will be doing the work yourself: building the models, writing the equipment specs, running the vendor evaluations, and standing in the building during commissioning. As the factories come online you will define, hire, and lead the industrialization and manufacturing engineering team that supports them. We are looking for someone who is genuinely happy in both modes and who wants to build the organization they will eventually run.

 You will report to the Vice President of Manufacturing and work most closely with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing, who owns the processes and product maturity you will be industrializing, and with the Plant Manager of each new facility, who owns the site once it is operating. You will also partner continuously with Pilot Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Technical Program Management, Digital Thread, Facilities, Finance, EHS, and Marine Operations.

 Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Responsibilities 

 Manufacturing Strategy and Industrialization Planning 

 
 Own the industrialization roadmap that takes each product and process from pilot production to qualified rate production.

 Build and maintain the manufacturing capacity and cost models that drive line decisions, including takt time, station balance, throughput, yield assumptions, unit cost, and capital intensity per unit of annual capacity.

 Partner with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing to define the build strategy for major structures and subsystems, including work breakdown, station sequencing, subassembly strategy, and heavy lift and transport requirements, bringing the rate-production perspective to processes proven in pilot.

 Partner with Supply Chain on make-versus-buy and internal-versus-contract-manufacturing decisions for major process steps, contributing the capacity, capital, process capability, and cycle-time analysis that informs them.

 Contribute manufacturing requirements to site selection and facility planning, including footprint, bay dimensions and door clearances, floor loading, crane and heavy lift capacity, laydown area, load-out access, and utility loads. Site selection is led by company leadership; you provide the manufacturing analysis and requirements that inform it.

 Develop facility layouts and material flow plans that support the target rate and future expansion.

 Provide manufacturability feedback to engineering, and drive design changes that reduce cost, cycle time, and process risk before they are locked in.

 
 Process, Tooling, and Equipment 

 
 Own the production equipment strategy and the major equipment list for each line, including welding and joining systems, automation and material handling, machining, coating, NDT and inspection, electronic rack assembly, panel wiring, hardware integration, and test infrastructure.

 Lead equipment specification, vendor evaluation, technical bid comparison, and selection in partnership with Pilot Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Quality.

 Define and manage the manufacturing capital plan, including budgets, phasing, long-lead-item strategy, and contingency, and present capital requests for approval.

 Transfer proven processes, work instructions, tooling, and training material out of pilot manufacturing and into the new lines, working with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing rather than reinventing what already works.

 Define tooling, fixture, and station design requirements and sequence their development against the installation schedule.

 Manage equipment vendors through design review, factory acceptance testing, delivery, installation, and site acceptance testing.

 
 Installation, Commissioning, and Qualification 

 
 Own the integrated installation and commissioning schedule for each line, from facility handover through equipment installation, utility tie-in, commissioning, process qualification, and first article.

 Define and drive the manufacturing critical path, including long-lead equipment, contractor sequencing, and dependencies on product and process readiness.

 Establish operational readiness criteria and lead readiness reviews with Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, and the incoming Plant Manager.

 Define the production system requirements the line needs at startup, including ERP, MES, and quality system needs, and partner with Digital Thread and enterprise systems teams on their delivery.

 Identify, track, and retire manufacturing schedule and technical risk with clear owners, mitigations, and escalation paths.

 
 Production Ramp 

 
 Define the manufacturing ramp curve for each line, including rate milestones, yield and learning-curve assumptions, labor ramp and training requirements, and staffing plan by station, in partnership with Technical Program Management and Production Planning.

 Set the readiness criteria that gate each step of the ramp and hold the line on them when schedule pressure builds.

 Establish the baseline process metrics, reporting cadence, and problem-solving mechanisms the Plant Manager will operate with.

 Lead a clean, documented handoff to the Plant Manager, and stay engaged as a partner through the ramp to rate.

 Capture lessons learned from each startup and apply them to the next line.

 
 Team Building and Organizational Development 

 
 Define the industrialization and manufacturing engineering org needed to support production at scale, including roles, sequencing of hires, and the split between central and site-based engineering.

 Recruit, hire, and develop that team, and set its technical standards, operating cadence, and priorities.

 Build the review mechanisms that keep industrialization work rigorous and visible, including design reviews, readiness reviews, and capital approval processes.

 Mentor engineers across manufacturing and grow bench strength for future factory startups.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 10+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, industrialization, or manufacturing operations, including time in a technical leadership role.

 Direct experience taking a product or process from prototype or pilot production through installation, qualification, and rate production.

 Demonstrated ownership of a manufacturing capital plan, including equipment specification, vendor selection, budgeting, and installation and commissioning schedules.

 Strong quantitative skills and fluency building capacity, cost, and ramp models that leadership can make decisions on.

 Experience defining and executing a production ramp, including realistic yield and learning-curve assumptions and the discipline to gate progress on readiness.

 Experience translating product designs into executable build strategies, process documentation, and station-level work content.

 Willingness to operate as a hands-on individual contributor now and build a team later, with genuine interest in both.

 Experience leading through influence across engineering, supply chain, quality, and site operations without direct authority over most of it.

 Clear written and verbal communication, and the judgment to know which decisions need a model, which need a conversation, and which need to be escalated.

 Comfort operating with incomplete information in a fast-moving environment where the product is still maturing.

 
 Desired Qualifications 

 
 Experience industrializing large welded steel structures, pressure-retaining assemblies, marine vessels, or comparable large-format fabricated hardware.

 Experience with waterfront manufacturing, shipyard or fabrication yard operations, or load-out and launch of large assemblies.

 Experience scaling from prototype or pilot production into volume manufacturing at a hardware startup.

 Experience hiring and building a manufacturing engineering or industrialization team from a small base.

 Experience selecting and deploying automation, robotic welding, or large-envelope machining and inspection systems.

 Familiarity with enterprise systems that support production, including PLM, ERP, MRP, MES, and QMS, and what they need to do at line startup.

 Experience with contract manufacturers, including qualification, technology transfer, and rate readiness.

 Experience in high-consequence or capital-intensive industries such as aerospace, defense, energy, shipbuilding, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 Working knowledge of facility and industrial infrastructure requirements for heavy manufacturing, including utilities, material handling, and layout and flow design.

 
 The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

 Skills and Competencies 

 
 High ownership and a bias toward delivery over analysis for its own sake.

 Ability to move between a spreadsheet model, a shop floor, and a leadership discussion in the same day.

 Rigor about assumptions, and willingness to state them plainly and revise them publicly.

 Ability to build trust quickly with plant leadership, trades, vendors, and contractors.

 Sound judgment about where to spend capital and where to spend ingenuity instead.

 Commitment to safety and quality as prerequisites for rate, not tradeoffs against it.

 
 Additional Requirements 

 
 This role requires regular on-site presence in Portland, Oregon, and at our pilot and contract manufacturing facility in Vancouver, Washington.

 Significant travel is expected, including to equipment vendors, contract manufacturers, candidate sites, and new facilities under construction. Travel will be heaviest during equipment procurement and startup phases and may include international travel.

 Comfort working across office, lab, fabrication, construction, and waterfront environments, with personal protective equipment required in designated areas.

 Ability to work extended or off-shift hours intermittently during commissioning, startup, and other time-critical operational windows.

 
 Compensation and Benefits 

 If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

 
 Cash compensation of $215,000 - $290,000.

 Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

 A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including:
 
 Flexible paid time off

 Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled)

 Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

 


 Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

 
 Location 

 This is an on-site position with expectation of regular presence in our Portland, Oregon facilities and at our Vancouver, Washington pilot manufacturing site. This position requires substantial domestic and international travel in support of equipment procurement, commissioning, and new facility startups.

 Exceptional remote candidates willing to spend at least 50% of their time in Portland are encouraged to apply.

records.title: Head of Quality
records.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.
This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

Requirements
You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
You have taken a product through product safety certification
You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so
Nice to haves
Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
Experience with manufacturing execution systems
Benefits
Fully employer-covered health insurance , so you’re protected without the premium.
A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.
Compensation
The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.
As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.
Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

records.title: Director of Quality
records.description:
Company Overview
ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments.

Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community.

Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security.

ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com http://allencontrolsystems.com.




Position Overview
We're looking for a Director of Quality to build our quality function from the ground up — including our path toward ISO 9001 — and lead it for the long haul. This role sets the multi-year quality strategy while staying grounded in what's really happening on the floor, in the supply base, and with customers. Our hardware matters; defects here aren't abstract metrics. Our core philosophy is quality at the source: quality can't be inspected in after the fact, it has to be built right the first time. QA is the backstop, not the primary defense — an escape that reaches the customer is a production failure, not a QA failure.
We want a pragmatic leader who favors simple, practical problem-solving (5 Whys, direct observation) over paperwork-heavy processes, and who will build a genuine partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers to catch issues at the source rather than at receiving.

What You'll Do:

Strategic & Long-Range Leadership
• Own the long-range quality strategy, translating business goals into a multi-year plan for systems, staffing, and capability.
• Architect our Quality Management System — including our path toward ISO 9001 — from the ground up, building processes that are clear and simple, not just audit-ready.
• Own the audit calendar as the QMS matures, treating findings as strategic input, not a checkbox.
• Set and report quality KPIs (defect rates, first-pass yield, complaints, supplier performance); a data point is noise, a trend is a signal.
• Put every requirement, gate, and approval on trial — if no one can name who owns it and why it exists, that's the signal to cut it, not preserve it.

Ground Truth & Root Cause
• Get out onto the floor, into supplier facilities, and in front of customers regularly — not just working from what's reported up the chain.
• Personally lead or coach RCCA using practical, lightweight tools (5 Whys, direct observation) instead of heavy formal methodologies when they aren't warranted.
• Move with urgency: default to “why can't this be fixed today,” not “when can we fit this in.”

Supply Chain & Supplier Quality
• Build a close partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers, treating supplier quality as a shared mission.
• Drive supplier qualification, scorecards, and joint problem-solving to resolve issues at the source.
• Serve as the primary quality point of contact for DCMA surveillance, audits, and findings.

Stakeholder Relationships
• Partner especially closely with Engineering and Manufacturing — closing the loop between field/production issues and design decisions, and keeping quality and throughput goals aligned.
• Own key external customer relationships on quality matters, building credibility through transparency and follow-through.

Team & Culture
• Manage, mentor, and develop the quality team with a bias toward action and practical problem-solving.
• Keep the QMS lean — every process should exist because it supports a real decision, not because it looks good on paper.
• Own customer complaints and non-conformances through to true root cause and permanent corrective action.

What You'll Need:
• 8+ years in quality leadership, ideally in manufacturing, hardware, or defense/aerospace.
• Experience building or scaling a QMS; ISO 9001 experience strongly preferred (we are not yet certified — you'll help drive us there).
• A track record of practical, tool-light RCCA (5 Whys, direct observation) over heavyweight, paperwork-driven processes.
• Experience partnering closely with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers.
• Comfort operating at both strategic altitude and on the floor — this is a hands-on role, not a desk job.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to influence engineering, manufacturing, and executive leadership alike.

What We Offer

 - Competitive salary

 - ACS Equity Package

 - Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

 - Paid Time Off

Allen Control Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer, providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment. Allen Control Systems prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

records.title: Sr. Manager, Production Planning & Scheduling
records.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

We're hiring our first Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling to own the factory side execution. Where our S&OP function decides where and whether we can build across the network, you own how and when it actually gets built on the floor. You'll own discrete operational scheduling, job sequencing and priority, and the daily/weekly rhythm that ensures on-time delivery (OTD) and sets the factory up for success.

This role reports to our Operations leadership and drives a consistent scheduling methodology across the network, while partnering closely with each site General Manager on execution. Your scheduling and planning team members will support the sites day-to-day (dotted-line to the GM) while you own the standards, methodology, and rigor centrally.

This is a builder and owner role. While the team is built out, you'll be hands-on developing the scheduling methodologies, communication rigor, and visual management that don't exist yet, and turning them into standard work. You'll be the person the floor, Program Management, and leadership rely on for a clear, credible answer to "what are we running, in what order, and are we going to hit the date?"

You'll partner tightly with the S&OP function, translating network-level allocation and capacity plans into an executable factory schedule — and feeding real execution signal back up to highlight and drive capacity improvements.

What You'll Do:

Own Production Scheduling & Execution

· Own discrete production scheduling and job sequencing across work centers to maximize on-time delivery and throughput.

· Own work order release to the floor and control what work is released and when.

· Set and manage priority and milestone dates, establish clear, transparent rules for what runs when, and make the trade-off calls when priorities conflict.

· Own data integrity for schedules and dates in the system, and maintain and drive accurate MRP schedules so plans, priorities, and downstream commitments can be trusted.

· Build the daily/weekly scheduling cadence and standard work that keeps the floor aligned, from shift-level execution to weekly look-ahead.

· Translate S&OP network allocation and capacity plans into an executable, sequenced factory schedule.

· Partner closely with the site General Manager to align on priorities, sequencing, and daily execution serving as the GM's right hand for turning the plan into on-time output.

· Establish the system and cadence for tracking work order progress through the floor, monitors status against milestone dates, surfaces at risk jobs early, and drives rapid recovery on exceptions.

Drive OTD & Factory Performance

 - Own on time delivery as a primary metric track it, root cause misses, and close the gaps.

 - Ensure the factory is set up for success: materials, tooling, capacity, and priorities aligned ahead of the work, not discovered at the machine.

 - Highlight and drive capacity improvements — surface constraints and bottlenecks from real execution data and partner with Operations and Engineering to resolve them.

 - Feed execution signal (actual cycle times, constraints, attainment) back to S&OP to sharpen capacity models and sellable-capacity commitments.

Build Methodology, Rigor & Visibility

 - Develop the scheduling methodologies and logic from the ground up, sequencing rules, buffering, prioritization frameworks and codify them as standard work applied consistently across sites.

 - Establish communication rigor: the meeting cadence, escalation paths, and reporting that keep the floor, the GMs, and leadership on the same page.

 - Build the visual management schedules, boards, dashboards, and status views that make factory status, priorities, and risks obvious at a glance.

 - Establish key scheduling metrics: OTD, schedule adherence, past due, work center utilization, and cycle time performance.

People Leadership

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planners and schedulers as the function scales, including team members embedded at and dotted lined to the sites.

 - Build organizational capability through talent development, standard work, training, and performance management.

 - Foster a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

· Proven experience in production planning, scheduling, or shop floor operations management in a discrete manufacturing environment.

· Deep understanding of production scheduling, sequencing, priority management, master scheduling, capacity/constraint analysis, and OTD drivers.

· Hands on experience with scheduling/ERP/MES systems and strong analytical and data visualization skills.

· Experience leading teams and developing planning/scheduling talent.

· Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to drive urgency and accountability on the floor.

· ERP/MRP expertise work order lifecycle, MRP mechanics, and maintaining schedule/date data integrity at scale.

Education & Experience Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline preferred.

 - 5+ years of progressive experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

records.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



Role Summary

The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build.

This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for.

From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of.

The intent behind housing this role in Build Engineering is clean accountability: your team scopes what we commit to, and Build Engineering delivers it. That means the commitments you shape have to be grounded in first-principles engineering judgment and a real understanding of the factory, not optimism. You evaluate and understand before you propose or promise.


Key Responsibilities

 - Represent Hadrian with customers day to day: Own the technical relationship with customer engineering, program, and leadership teams. Run working sessions, present findings and recommendations, handle hard questions and pushback in the room, and follow up with clear, accurate written communication. Every interaction should leave the customer more confident in Hadrian.

 - Discover before you design: Embed with customers to observe their operations, map processes, constraints, and pain points, and interview stakeholders from the shop floor to program leadership. Build a clear, evidence-based picture of the real need before any solution is on the table.

 - Shape the solution: Fold what you learn into a solution that maximizes customer output and moves Hadrian toward what we are building. Hold an accurate picture of current capability and roadmap, and steer each engagement to the point where those two goals reinforce each other, favoring existing capabilities over new obligations.

 - Partner with Customer Programs: Operate on a dotted line to Customer Programs as their forward deployed engineering arm, bringing technical judgment into every engagement from first conversation through commitment.

 - Lead the forward deployed engineering team: Build, manage, and develop a technical team that engages directly with customers during new program scoping. Set the standard for how the team runs discovery, evaluates opportunities, and communicates with customers in a technical, credible, low-ego way.

 - Scope new customer engagements: Own the manufacturing scoping of new engagements: review requirements, drawings, specifications, tolerances, materials, and volumes, and define a manufacturing solution that Hadrian can commit to with confidence.

 - Evaluate before you promise: Bring a first-principles engineering mindset to every engagement. Understand the problem and the constraints before proposing or committing to a solution, so that what we sign up for is real and deliverable.

 - Hand off cleanly to Build Engineering: Ensure every commitment is scoped so that the Build Engineering organization can deliver it: clear product definition, make-vs-buy posture, process capability requirements, and a manufacturing plan that stands up to execution.

 - Drive leverage, not one-offs: Recognize recurring customer patterns and turn them into repeatable scoping approaches and reusable solution templates, so the function scales with the business instead of scaling headcount linearly.
   

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field and 8+ years of manufacturing or manufacturing engineering experience, or 12+ years of that experience without a degree.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Background spanning both a scaling/startup environment and a mature manufacturing organization.

 - Exposure to precision machining, castings, forgings, sheet metal, or additive processes across metals and composites.

Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Head of Manufacturing Engineering to lead the development and scale-up of our manufacturing systems for high-volume small unmanned aircraft production. This leader will own the manufacturing engineering organization responsible for translating product designs into robust, automated, production-ready manufacturing systems capable of operating reliably at scale.

A major focus of this role will be factory automation, controls engineering, equipment development, and manufacturing systems architecture. You will build and lead a multidisciplinary organization spanning manufacturing engineering, automation and controls, equipment engineering, process development, and production industrialization.

The ideal candidate has experience scaling complex electromechanical products from early production into high-rate manufacturing, with a strong understanding of how automation, controls, data, equipment design, and process engineering come together to create a world-class production system.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can establish the long-term manufacturing strategy while also driving execution on the factory floor.



How You’ll Make an Impact:

 - Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Manufacturing Engineering organization supporting production from new product introduction through high-volume manufacturing.

 - Define the manufacturing engineering strategy, technical roadmap, organizational structure, and capabilities required to support significant production growth.

 - Partner closely with Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Test Engineering, and Product teams to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, automation, testability, and scale.

 - Establish manufacturing standards, design reviews, equipment specifications, process qualification methodologies, and production-readiness criteria.

 - Lead the architecture, development, deployment, and lifecycle management of automated manufacturing equipment and production systems.

 - Build strong internal capabilities in controls engineering, PLC programming, industrial robotics, motion control, machine vision, industrial networking, sensors, servo systems, safety systems, and automated material handling.

 - Partner with software and data teams to connect manufacturing equipment with MES, traceability, quality, and factory data systems.

What Makes You a Good Fit:

 - 5+ years of experience leading engineering organizations responsible for manufacturing systems or factory automation.

 - Demonstrated experience scaling complex electromechanical products into high-volume production.

   - Servo and motion-control systems

   - Industrial networking and communications
   
   - Sensors and instrumentation
   
   - Automated test and inspection
   
   - Machine safety systems
   
   - SCADA/HMI systems

 - Experience operating in environments requiring rigorous configuration management, traceability, process control, and quality systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and lead multidisciplinary technical organizations.

About the Role:

The NPI Operations Engineering leader builds and leads the team responsible for making Skydio's next generation of autonomous robotics, including drones, docks and accessories, at our internal manufacturing facility in Hayward. You’ll deliver the process, manufacturing know-how and technology needed to build the most capable flying robots on the planet. The team combines Manufacturing Design Engineering and Supply Base Engineering into one organization that is 100% focused on new product development.

You will own the manufacturability of every new product: assembly time, assembly yield and the processes, fixtures, equipment and supplier readiness needed to hit them. You and your team will engage with Product Engineering from early architecture, carry products through EVT, DVT and PVT, and hand them to Process Engineering for sustaining once they meet clear production-readiness criteria.

This is a leadership role with significant scope to shape how Skydio develops hardware. You'll set the team's direction, hire and grow engineers, and be the single operations voice in product development. Sustaining engineering for products already in production sits with Process Engineering, so this team stays focused on getting new products right before they reach the line.



How You’ll Make an Impact:


OWN MANUFACTURABILITY OF NEW PRODUCTS

 - Own the operations engineering development for NPI programs across supply chain and in-house manufacturing

 - Drive design-for-manufacturing, assembly and serviceability (DFx) input from early architecture onward

 - Set and commit to assembly time and assembly yield targets for each new product, and track them at every build

 - Own operations sign-off at product development gates, and escalate manufacturability risks with clear trade-offs

 - Use PFMEA, DFM reviews and prototype yield, quality and process data to align product design with manufacturing strategy

 - Identify manufacturing risks early and drive mitigation plans to closure before production ramp


LEAD NPI EXECUTION THROUGH PRODUCTION READINESS

 - Own the manufacturing plan for new products and major design changes, from prototype through PVT

 - Define assembly flow, line layout, fixtures and equipment for new products, with labor, cost and capacity estimates that sharpen at each build

 - Coordinate engineering, design and production validation builds with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Test and Quality

 - Define production-readiness and handoff criteria, and lead manufacturing readiness reviews

 - Develop and continuously improve Skydio's NPI process

 - Transfer products to Process Engineering with complete documentation, released tooling, and yield and cycle time at target


DEVELOP PROCESSES, FIXTURES AND ASSEMBLY EQUIPMENT

 - Own development and validation of assembly processes, including mechanical assembly, electronics integration, adhesive bonding, fastening, soldering and calibration

 - Own design and qualification of assembly fixtures, error-proofing, and assembly equipment such as dispense systems and torque-controlled drivers

 - Own the capital budget for new-product assembly fixtures and equipment. Capital for the running production line stays with Manufacturing

 - Develop process specifications, control plans, component and assembly CTQs, inspections, inline tests, work instructions and manufacturing BOMs, all complete before handoff

 - Use statistical process control (SPC), capability studies and structured experiments to establish robust process windows


DEVELOP CORE MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGIES

 - Build a roadmap of core process technologies that future products depend on, such as waterproofing and ingress protection, conformal coatings, sealing and advanced bonding

 - Partner with material suppliers, equipment vendors and technology partners to develop, qualify and industrialize these processes ahead of product need

 - Serve as the technical owner for these technologies after production launch


LEAD SUPPLY BASE ENGINEERING FOR NEW PRODUCTS

 - Drive supplier selection, part qualification and supplier process readiness for new products

 - Own NPI automation at the process level during development, and partner with the Factory Automation team for production handoff

 - Work with suppliers on component DFM, process capability, capacity and quality before production launch

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Quality on make-versus-buy decisions, supplier development and capital business cases


LEAD AND BUILD THE TEAM

 - Set the vision, strategy and execution plan for NPI Operations Engineering

 - Lead, hire and develop a team of manufacturing design engineers and supply base engineers, acting as the team's lead technical expert and mentor

 - Integrate MDE and SBE into one team with shared programs, goals and ways of working

 - Set priorities and staffing across multiple concurrent programs and SKUs at different stages, working with leaders across the company to understand build targets and focus the team on hitting them

 - Protect the team's focus on new products, with a clean handoff to Process Engineering for sustaining

 - Build an inclusive, diverse, engaged and high-performing team through a mix of external hiring and developing internal talent, with regular coaching and growth opportunities

 - Build a culture of technical rigor, ownership and close partnership with design engineering


COLLABORATION

 - Work closely with Product Engineering leaders on airframes, propulsion, cameras, sensors, batteries, gimbals and payloads

 - Align with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Test Engineering and Automation Engineering on capacity, equipment and handoff plans

 - Communicate program status, risks and manufacturability trade-offs clearly to executive leadership
   
   

What Makes You a Good Fit:

 - Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial or Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

 - 10+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, NPI or production engineering for complex electromechanical products, ideally including high-volume production.

 - [4+] years leading engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers [and managers].

 - A track record of taking multiple complex hardware products from early development into high-quality production.

 - Deep expertise in DFM/DFA and a history of influencing product design early, not only fixing problems at the build.

 - Hands-on fixture design experience, and a strong understanding of factory lines, assembly flow and how to optimize them.

 - SPC, Lean and Six Sigma experience.

 - Experience working with suppliers on part qualification, process capability and production readiness.

 - Strong data skills: you set yield, cycle-time and cost targets, measure them and use the data to drive decisions.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, working collaboratively with people at every level, from technicians to executive leadership.

 - Strong project management, analytical skills and attention to detail, with sound independent judgment on complex, broad-scope problems.

 - Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving products, and willingness to be on the floor during critical builds.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.


NICE TO HAVE

postedPay.text: This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office.  The target base pay for this position is $190,000- $225,000annually.  The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

records.description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. 


The VP, Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q) holds the independent oversight authority that ensures every spacecraft is safe, reliable, and qualified before it launches. This role is structurally independent of all other VP organizations - the authority to halt work, reject deliverables, and withhold qualification sign-off cannot be overridden by any VP. Only the CTO can override an MA&Q determination, and that override is documented with the MA&Q position on record regardless of outcome.
 
Independence is the defining feature of this role. MA&Q does not build hardware, does not own schedule, and does not report to any VP who does. This structural separation is deliberate - quality and safety decisions must never be compromised by production pressure, schedule urgency, or cost targets.
 
The VP, MA&Q must be willing to halt a production line, delay a gate review, or withhold qualification sign-off when the evidence demands it - and hold that position under pressure from peers and the CTO alike.

What you’ll be doing:
Mission Assurance
Own the FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification -zero unmitigated single-point failures is a CDR entry criterion
Chair the Failure Review Board (FRB) -convene, lead root cause investigation, assess extent of condition, and close with verified corrective action
Define mission success criteria and own fault tree analysis
Safety
Implement and own the system safety program per MIL-STD-882 or program-equivalent standard
Lead hazard analysis (PHA, SHA) and maintain the hazard tracking log through every gate
Manage propulsion, battery, high-voltage, and deployment safety; provide range safety interface for launch operations
Quality Assurance
Exercise independent inspection authority across all program phases
Hold sole NCR disposition authority -Use-As-Is and Repair require MA&Q concurrence regardless of phase
Enforce workmanship standards per IPC-A-610 Class 3; conduct process audits and first article inspections
Issue Standing Disposition Authorizations (SDAs) for recurring Tier 2/3 NCRs; Tier 1 Critical NCRs trigger CTO notification within 4 hours
Reliability Engineering
Own quantitative reliability model per MIL-HDBK-217 or equivalent; track MTBF/MTTR targets against the constellation availability model
Lead reliability growth tracking, redundancy analysis, and reliability predictions correlated with test data at QR
Parts Engineering & Radiation
Maintain the Preferred Parts List (PPL) - sole authority to add or remove parts; no part may fly without PPL approval
Enforce derating compliance at CDR and manage lot acceptance testing
Specify the mission radiation environment (TID, SEE, displacement damage) and track radiation margins for all flight parts
Configuration Management
Chair the production CCB and administer the ECO/ECN process
Maintain as-built configuration records from the MES; execute FCA and PCA before Phase Close Gate
Provide as-built conformance report to the CTO
What you bring to this role:
15+ years of progressive mission assurance, quality engineering, or reliability engineering on flight programs; at least one spacecraft program carried from system requirements through on-orbit operations
Demonstrated record of exercising halt/reject authority or withholding qualification sign-off against schedule and cost pressure you must describe a specific instance. This is the most important qualification for the role
Direct accountability for a flight program's FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification, including enforcing zero-unmitigated-SPOF at CDR
Experience designing, implementing, and running a tiered NCR classification and disposition system at production rate, including Use-As-Is and Repair disposition authority
Direct experience chairing or co-chairing a spacecraft Qualification Review and making the independent go/no-go determination
Familiarity with PPL management, derating analysis, lot acceptance testing, and radiation qualification requirements (TID, SEE)
Demonstrated record of building multi-discipline assurance teams spanning all seven functions
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Systems, Electrical Engineering, or related field — or equivalent verifiable experience
Bonus Points for the Following
Direct experience with constellation programs and fleet-wide conformance reporting
Familiarity with SAP (Special Access Program) assurance requirements
Prior experience as CCB chair in a high-rate production environment
Familiarity with CMMI or AS9100 quality management systems in a space or defense manufacturing environment
Range safety certification or prior direct range safety interface experience
Additional Requirements

postedPay.title: Head of Operations Planning and Special Projects

records.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock's technology is scaling rapidly —over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners, and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform.  

The Head of Operations Planning & Special Projects owns aligning cross-functionally on an integrated machine plan across types, generations, product lines, partners, sites in order to develop Operational headcount and material plans; ultimately, giving the business a clear view of what's required and by when. 

You'll own the integrated machine plan, scenario planning, cross-functional alignment when constraints arise, building headcount scaling factors and plans, and standing up our early Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Reporting to the VP of Operations, you'll be a critical thought partner to the VP and each Operations Lead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


INTEGRATED PLANNING

 - Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 - Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 - Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 - Support senior leadership and board-level decisions with clear, rigorous analysis.

 - Partner with the VP of Operations to define team OKRs, the mechanisms to track them, and routine reporting on critical initiatives.

 - Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 - Help align data collection needs with operational optimizations to strengthen our data pipelines.


S&OP PROCESS IMPLEMENTATION

 - Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to build stage-appropriate S&OP processes that tee up critical business decisions, surface constraints, and evaluate alternatives.

 - Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end: forecast development, demand review inputs, forecast analysis, supply plan integration, pre-meeting coordination, and reporting.

 - Forecast demand, assess whether projected supply can meet it, and define key performance metrics such as forecast accuracy and fulfillment rate.

 - Serve as the bridge between business strategy, engineering build plans, finance, and supply chain execution.


PRODUCTION PLANNING COORDINATION

 - Own phase-in / phase-out planning for new machine types, product lines, partners and sites, and hardware generations — including availability, supply constraints, retrofits, and partner transitions.

 - Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 - Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Contract Manufacturing to plan production capacity against demand, consolidate risks, and drive prioritization when supply is constrained.


OPERATIONS INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

 - Own the development of core operational metrics and routine reporting.

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to the business.

 - Support continuous improvement across Operations through process and data.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A single, trusted integrated plan that the business uses to make decisions about machines, people, and materials.

 - Constraints surfaced early, with clear scenarios and recommendations — not surprises.

 - A functioning monthly S&OP cadence with consistent participation and clear decisions.

 - Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - 8–10 years in operations, planning, or program leadership, including 5+ years working with cross-functional teams distributed across sites or regions.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence leaders — aligning cross-functional stakeholders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth.

 - Track record implementing S&OP or supply-and-demand processes that bring clarity to requirements, decisions, and success criteria.

 - Experience planning and managing hourly / field workforce headcount.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to turn data into operational decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including with executives.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with autonomy, heavy machinery, and/or the construction industry.

 - Experience standing up supply-and-demand review processes that clarify timelines, requirements, decisions, risks, and solutions.

 - Continuous improvement, Lean, or Six Sigma experience, including standing up an improvement program.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

As Bedrock scales, the hardest problems are increasingly about coordination: getting the right machines, people, and parts to the right sites at the right time. This role builds the planning backbone that lets every Operations team — and the company — make faster, better decisions with confidence.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

We’re looking for a hands-on manufacturing leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 

You will lead prototype build execution and the manufacturing setup of our new Seattle-area facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll build the production team, establish the factory’s operating system and deliver the readiness needed to scale aircraft production safely, reliably and efficiently.

   - Maintain configuration discipline and aircraft traceability throughout development builds in partnership with Engineering and Quality.

   - Lead manufacturing setup and operational readiness for X-Forge 3, working with Facilities and Manufacturing Engineering on factory layout, equipment installation, commissioning and production flow. 
   
   - Recruit, develop and lead the production organization, building capable frontline leadership and a skilled aircraft assembly team. 
   
   - Own production staffing, training and capacity plans, aligning investment and workforce growth with program demand. 
   
   - Drive launch readiness across people, tooling, materials, processes and quality, with clear owners and closure plans for gaps. 
   
   - Lead the transition from prototype operations into Seattle production, ensuring build knowledge and lessons learned transfer with the work. 
   
   Deliver and scale aircraft production 
   
   - Own production execution against safety, quality, delivery and cost targets as X-BAT moves through initial production and into sustained rate. 
   
   - Establish daily operating routines, visual management and escalation processes that surface problems early and drive timely resolution. 
   
   - Improve throughput, labor productivity, first-pass quality and schedule adherence through practical Lean methods and structured problem-solving. 
   
   - Partner with Supply Chain and Planning to align material availability, supplier readiness and outsourced manufacturing with the production plan. 
   
   - Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to eliminate recurring build issues and embed permanent corrective actions. 
   
   - Deploy digital manufacturing tools and appropriate automation to improve execution, traceability and scalability. 
   
   - Give leadership a clear view of production performance, launch readiness, risks and the decisions needed to maintain progress.

 - Demonstrated experience leading prototype or new product introduction builds and carrying a product into sustained production. 

 - Proven ability to build and scale manufacturing operations, including workforce development, capacity planning and production systems. 

 - Experience leading complex assembly and integration operations with demanding quality, configuration and traceability requirements. 

 - Strong understanding of manufacturing readiness, tooling validation, material coordination and production launch. 

 - Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery and cost through Lean manufacturing and structured problem-solving. 

 - Ability to lead across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Program Management, resolving competing priorities and driving clear accountability. 

 - A hands-on leadership style, with the ability to move between long-term factory planning and detailed problem-solving on the floor.

records.title: Sr. Staff Solutions Architect – Manufacturing (R6252)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies.
